part1_reVerificationOfPriorDetermination.claim: The prior phase's audit determined that 'different-base-section false matches' and 'bare/undifferentiated-section definitional overmatch' live ONLY in the frozen evaluator matcher (lib/contract-model/evaluation-v2/matching.ts / semantic-correspondence.ts), verified via zero production imports from evaluation-v2.
part1_reVerificationOfPriorDetermination.independentReVerificationMethod: Re-ran the exact grep independently this session: `grep -rn "evaluation-v2" lib/contract-model/compiler/` - zero matches (exit code 1, no match found). Also independently ran the permanent mechanical enforcement test tests/evaluation-v2/import-boundary.test.ts (5 tests) - all pass. Also independently read production's own three identity mechanisms end to end (identity.ts's computeSemanticUnitId/computeCoverageEntryId/computeFrozenContentHash, discovery/pass-c-neighborhood.ts's discoveryId formula, discovery/pass-d-reconcile.ts's mergeKey) and confirmed none of them share any code, matching heuristic, or string/section-ref-based correspondence logic with evaluation-v2/matching.ts or semantic-correspondence.ts - they are structurally independent hash-of-content-derived identity schemes, not string-similarity matchers of the evaluator's own shape.
part1_reVerificationOfPriorDetermination.independentDetermination: CONFIRMED - both named risks remain EVALUATOR-MATCHER-ONLY. This is an independent re-verification (own grep re-run, own import-boundary test execution, own reading of the production identity code), not a re-statement of the prior phase's own claim taken on faith.

part2_independentAdversarialConstruction.methodology: 8 adversarial fixtures, independently authored (never copied from tests/contract-model/discovery-pipeline.test.ts, though the same zero-cost SemanticRuleItem-construction technique that file already established is reused), run through the REAL production functions: runPassCNeighborhoodExpansion + runPassDReconciliation (lib/contract-model/compiler/discovery/**, using the ACTUAL discoveryId function those modules themselves return - never a re-derived stand-in) for candidateRef identity, and hypothesizeUnitsForDocument/routeDocument (lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-coverage/**) for semanticUnitId identity. No LLM call anywhere - SemanticRuleItem inputs are constructed directly, exactly as Pass B's own output shape, and fed straight into Pass C/D, which is real, unmodified production code.

part3_confirmedNewFinding.title: Production candidateRef/discoveryId identity DOES conflate two distinct sibling claims when they share a structural node and discovery role with no resolvable sub-reference (an un-enumerated multi-claim sentence)
part3_confirmedNewFinding.location: lib/contract-model/compiler/discovery/pass-c-neighborhood.ts (discoveryId = computeStableKey("discovery-candidate", documentId, normalizedSourceRef, role, discoveryRunVersion)) and pass-d-reconcile.ts (mergeKey = `${primaryNodeId}::${role}`)
part3_confirmedNewFinding.mechanism: When a single sentence states two independently-operative, economically distinct claims (e.g. 'the Company shall not create Liens on the Collateral or incur Indebtedness in excess of $10,000,000') with no lettered/numbered enumeration for Pass C to resolve a distinct sub-node ref against, BOTH claims' relativeRef resolution falls back to the SAME anchor (the enclosing section/clause node) with the SAME discovery role, producing the SAME discoveryId. Pass D's reconciliation then merges them into ONE DiscoveredCandidate under its own documented 'two candidates are merged only when they resolve to the EXACT same primary structural node AND the same role; anything else is kept distinct' rule - which is violated in spirit here, since the two items ARE textually distinct, independently-operative claims, not duplicate detections of the same claim. On merge, `byKey.set(mergeKey, {...existing, ...})` retains ONLY the first-seen candidate's own `description` field - the second claim's own description is silently discarded (a discrepancy from the merge code's own comment, 'keep the higher-confidence description', which the actual code does not implement - it always keeps `existing`'s description regardless of confidence).
part3_confirmedNewFinding.confirmedByDirectExecution: tests/foundation-audit/section15-claim-identity-adversarial.ts case 'same-section-different-claim-NO-markers': 2 authored claims -> 1 reconciled DiscoveredCandidate. Also independently confirmed at the Phase 3E semantic-coverage identity layer (semanticUnitId): the identical fused sentence run through the real hypothesizeUnitsForDocument produces exactly 1 MaterialSemanticUnit, not 2 - the SAME root cause (reliance on enumeration markers to split distinct claims) affects BOTH production identity mechanisms independently, not just discoveryId.
mitigatingFactorsFoundByCodeReading: `multipleRulesLikely` is correctly OR'd onto the merged candidate (true if EITHER original item flagged it), so the collision is disclosed on the surviving candidate, not silently hidden from any downstream consumer that checks this field.

The semantic compiler's own prompt (lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/prompt.ts line 39: 'MULTIPLE RULES: ... Emit one WireRule per independently operative rule - never merge distinct baskets into one') instructs multi-rule extraction from the FULL underlying source text (operativeSourceText, which is the section's own real raw text, not the discovery candidate's own possibly-lossy `description` field) - so a live model compilation MAY still recover both claims as two separate IRRules despite the discovery-layer merge. This specific recovery behavior could not be verified this session (no API key configured; the SyntheticStageCaller/SyntheticSemanticCaller fallback always returns zero rules and cannot exercise this judgment call) - disclosed as an unverifiable, live-model-dependent question rather than assumed to resolve the risk.

Downstream semantic-coverage reconciliation (reconciliation.ts's findAnchoredRule) matches individual claims by compiled-RULE citation, not by candidateRef, so IF the compiler does emit two distinct-citation IRRules under the one merged candidateRef, per-claim credit is still separable at the coverage-measurement layer.

verifiedCandidateRefs-based verification gating (semantic-coverage/reconciliation.ts) is per-candidateRef, which is CONSERVATIVE in this scenario, not permissive: if either claim under the merged candidate has an unresolved MATERIAL finding, the WHOLE candidateRef fails to reach FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED, so this collision cannot itself manufacture a false 'verified' credit - it can, at worst, under-credit a genuinely correct claim by coupling its verified status to its merged sibling's.
part3_confirmedNewFinding.scopeDistinctionFromPart1: This is a DIFFERENT, independently-discovered risk from the two evaluator-matcher-only risks re-verified in Part 1 above. It lives entirely in PRODUCTION code (discovery/pass-c-neighborhood.ts, discovery/pass-d-reconcile.ts, semantic-coverage/unit-hypothesis.ts) - it has no evaluation-v2 involvement at all - and is reported per this task's own explicit instruction to report such a finding honestly even where it diverges from the prior phase's own (differently-scoped) determination.
